plan: Psalm 47:1-9; Psalm 48:1-14; Psalm 49:1-20; Psalm 84:1-12; Psalm 85:1-13; Psalm 87:1-7

readings.section: The Psalms of the Sons of Korah
readings.title: The Sovereign Over the Nations
readings.subtitle: Acknowledging the ultimate administrative control of YeHoVaH over the physical realm.
readings.text: [Psalm 47:1] Oh, clap your hands, all you peoples! Shout to <dn>Elohim</dn> with a voice of singing! [2] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> Most High is awesome; A great Sovereign over all the earth. [3] <dn>He</dn> subdues <dn>את</dn> peoples under us, And <dn>את</dn> nations under our feet. [4] <dn>He</dn> chooses <dn>את</dn> our inheritance for us, The excellence of Ya‘aqoḇ whom <dn>He</dn> loves. Selah.

readings.section: The Psalms of the Sons of Korah
readings.title: The Set-Apart Throne
readings.subtitle: The gathering of nations under the singular, uncontained essence of the Creator.
readings.text: [5] <dn>Elohim</dn> shall go up with a shout, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with a voice of a shophar. [6] Sing praises to <dn>Elohim</dn>, sing praises! Sing praises to our Sovereign, sing praises! [7] For <dn>Elohim</dn> is Sovereign of all the earth; Sing praises with understanding. [8] <dn>Elohim</dn> shall reign over the nations; <dn>Elohim</dn> shall sit on <dn>His</dn> set-apart throne. [9] Nobles of peoples shall be gathered together, The people of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Aḇraham. For the shields of the earth belong to <dn>Elohim</dn>; <dn>He</dn> shall be greatly exalted.

readings.section: The Psalms of the Sons of Korah
readings.title: The Ultimate Administrative Capital
readings.subtitle: Mount Tsiyon established as the structural joy and refuge of the physical earth.
readings.text: [Psalm 48:1] Great is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and greatly to be praised In the city of our <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>His</dn> set-apart mountain. [2] Beautiful on high, The joy of all the earth, Is Mount Tsiyon on the sides of the north, The city of the great Sovereign. [3] <dn>Elohim</dn> is in her citadels; <dn>He</dn> is known as her refuge.

readings.section: The Psalms of the Sons of Korah
readings.title: The Overthrow of Rebellious Sovereigns
readings.subtitle: The adversary's systems fracture before the enduring establishment of Elohim's city.
readings.text: [4] For look, the sovereigns met, They passed by together. [5] They saw, so they marvelled; They were alarmed, they hastened away. [6] Trembling took hold of them there, Pain, as of a woman in labour, [7] With an east wind <dn>You</dn> break <dn>את</dn> the ships of Tarshish. [8] As we have heard, so we have seen In the city of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, In the city of our <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>Elohim</dn> establishes <dn>את</dn> her forever. Selah.

readings.section: The Psalms of the Sons of Korah
readings.title: The Right Arm of Justice
readings.subtitle: Rejoicing in the right-rulings executed by the Right Arm of YeHoVaH across generations.
readings.text: [9] We have thought, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, of <dn>Your</dn> loving-commitment, In the midst of <dn>Your</dn> Hĕḵal. [10] According to <dn>Your</dn> Name, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, So is <dn>Your</dn> praise to the ends of the earth; <dn>Your</dn> right hand is filled with righteousness. [11] Let Mount Tsiyon rejoice, Let the daughters of Yehuḏah exult, Because of <dn>Your</dn> right-rulings. [12] Walk about Tsiyon, And go all around her. Count <dn>את</dn> her towers; [13] Set <dn>את</dn> your heart upon her rampart; Go through her citadels; So that you report it to the coming generation. [14] For this <dn>Elohim</dn> is our <dn>Elohim</dn>, Forever and ever; <dn>He</dn> <dn>Himself</dn> leads us, Even to death.

readings.section: The Psalms of the Sons of Korah
readings.title: A Riddle for the World
readings.subtitle: A call for structural understanding regarding the transitory nature of mankind.
readings.text: [Psalm 49:1] Hear this, all you peoples; Give ear, all you inhabitants of the world, [2] Both sons of mankind and sons of man, Rich and poor together. [3] My mouth speaks wisdom, And the meditation of my heart brings understanding. [4] I incline my ear to a parable; I expound my riddle on the lyre.

readings.section: The Psalms of the Sons of Korah
readings.title: The Inability to Ransom Life
readings.subtitle: Exposing the fatal flaw of the adversary's economic system in the face of the ultimate cosmic verdict.
readings.text: [5] Why should I fear in the days of evil, When the crookedness of my supplanters surrounds me? [6] Those who are trusting in their riches And who are boasting in their great wealth? [7] A brother does not redeem <dn>את</dn> anyone at all, Neither give to <dn>Elohim</dn> a ransom for him; [8] For the redemption of their lives is costly, And it shall cease forever; [9] That he should still live forever, And not see the pit. [10] For he sees wise men die, The foolish and the ignorant both perish, And shall leave their wealth to others. [11] Their inner thoughts are their houses, forever; Their dwelling places, to all generations; They call their lands after their own names. [12] But man does not remain in esteem, He is like the beasts that perish.

readings.section: The Psalms of the Sons of Korah
readings.title: Redemption from the Pit
readings.subtitle: While the followers of Babel face terminal consumption, the righteous are redeemed by Elohim's power.
readings.text: [Psalm 49:13] This way of theirs is folly to them, Yet their followers are pleased with their words. Selah. [14] Like sheep they shall be laid in She’ol; Death shall shepherd them; And the upright rule over them in the morning; And their form is consumed in She’ol, Far from their dwelling. [15] But <dn>Elohim</dn> does redeem <dn>את</dn> my being From the power of She’ol, For <dn>He</dn> does receive <dn>את</dn> me. Selah.

readings.section: The Psalms of the Sons of Korah
readings.title: The Terminal State of Ignorance
readings.subtitle: The ultimate lack of inheritance for those operating outside the covenants of YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [16] Do not be afraid when a man becomes rich, When the wealth of his house increases; [17] For when he dies he takes none of it; His wealth does not go down after him. [18] Though while he lived he blessed himself, And though they praise you when you do well for yourself, [19] He has to go to the generation of his fathers; They never see the light. [20] Man, who is rich, Yet does not understand, Shall be like the beasts, They shall perish.

readings.section: The Psalms of the Sons of Korah
readings.title: Longing for the Divine Courts
readings.subtitle: A visceral yearning to abide in the functional presence and legislative courts of the Living Ěl.
readings.text: [Psalm 84:1] How lovely are <dn>Your</dn> dwelling places, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts! [2] My being has longed, and even fainted, For the courts of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>; My heart and my flesh cry out for the living <dn>Ěl</dn>. [3] Even the sparrow has found a home, And the swallow a nest for herself, Where she has put her young ones – <dn>Your</dn> slaughter-places, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, My Sovereign and my <dn>Elohim</dn>. [4] Blessed are those who dwell in <dn>Your</dn> house, They are ever praising <dn>You</dn>. Selah.

readings.section: The Psalms of the Sons of Korah
readings.title: Strength in the Covenant Highways
readings.subtitle: Transforming the physical struggle into a fountain of blessing through absolute trust in YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [5] Blessed is the man whose strength is in <dn>You</dn>, <dn>Your</dn> Highways are in their heart. [6] Passing through the valley of weeping, They make it a fountain; The Teacher also covers it with blessings. [7] They go from strength to strength, Appearing before <dn>Elohim</dn> in Tsiyon. [8] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of hosts, hear my prayer; Give ear, O <dn>Elohim</dn> of Ya‘aqoḇ! Selah.

readings.section: The Psalms of the Sons of Korah
readings.title: The Ultimate Rest and Shield
readings.subtitle: Recognizing YeHoVaH as the singular source of physical protection and unmerited favor for the upright.
readings.text: [9] O <dn>Elohim</dn>, see <dn>את</dn> our shield, And look upon <dn>את</dn> the face of <dn>Your</dn> anointed. [10] For a day in <dn>Your</dn> courts Is better than a thousand days. I have chosen rather to be a doorkeeper In the House of my <dn>Elohim</dn>, Than to dwell in the tents of the wrong. [11] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> is a sun and a shield; <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gives favour and esteem; <dn>He</dn> withholds no good matter From those who walk blamelessly. [12] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, Blessed is the man who trusts in <dn>You</dn>!

readings.section: The Psalms of the Sons of Korah
readings.title: Turning Back Captivity
readings.subtitle: The restorative act of YeHoVaH to cover the crookedness of His covenant people.
readings.text: [Psalm 85:1] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>You</dn> shall take pleasure in <dn>Your</dn> land; <dn>You</dn> shall turn back <dn>את</dn> the captivity of Ya‘aqoḇ. [2] <dn>You</dn> shall take away <dn>את</dn> the crookedness of <dn>Your</dn> people; <dn>You</dn> shall cover <dn>את</dn> all their sin. Selah. [3] <dn>You</dn> shall withdraw all <dn>Your</dn> wrath; <dn>You</dn> shall turn from <dn>Your</dn> fierce displeasure.

readings.section: The Psalms of the Sons of Korah
readings.title: A Plea for Revival
readings.subtitle: Appealing to the foundational loving-commitment of Elohim for national deliverance.
readings.text: [4] Turn back to us, O <dn>Elohim</dn> of our deliverance, And cause <dn>Your</dn> vexation toward us to cease. [5] Would <dn>You</dn> be enraged with us forever? Would <dn>You</dn> draw out <dn>Your</dn> displeasure From generation to generation? [6] Would <dn>You</dn> not revive us again, For <dn>Your</dn> people to rejoice in <dn>You</dn>? [7] Show us <dn>Your</dn> loving-commitment, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, And give us <dn>Your</dn> deliverance.

readings.section: The Psalms of the Sons of Korah
readings.title: The Convergence of Justice and Truth
readings.subtitle: The precise alignment of Emunah (Truth) and Tsedek (Justice) to establish a functioning, harmonious cosmos.
readings.text: [8] Let me hear what <dn>Ěl</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> speaks, For <dn>He</dn> speaks peace to <dn>His</dn> people And to <dn>His</dn> lovingly-committed ones; And let them not turn again to folly. [9] Truly, <dn>His</dn> deliverance is near to those who fear <dn>Him</dn>, For esteem to dwell in our land. [10] Loving-commitment and truth shall meet, Righteousness and peace shall kiss. [11] Truth sprouts forth from the earth, And righteousness looks down from heaven, [12] Indeed, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gives <dn>את</dn> what is good, And our land yields its increase. [13] Righteousness goes before <dn>Him</dn>, And prepares a way for <dn>His</dn> footsteps.

readings.section: The Psalms of the Sons of Korah
readings.title: The Gates of Tsiyon
readings.subtitle: The geographic epicenter chosen by YeHoVaH as the foundation for His eternal city.
readings.text: [Psalm 87:1] <dn>His</dn> foundation is In the set-apart mountains. [2] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> loves <dn>את</dn> the gates of Tsiyon More than all the dwellings of Ya‘aqoḇ. [3] Esteemed matters are spoken of you, O city of <dn>Elohim</dn>: Selah.

readings.section: The Psalms of the Sons of Korah
readings.title: The Registry of Nations
readings.subtitle: The official recording of the overcomers integrated into the physical and spiritual lineage of Tsiyon.
readings.text: [4] <dq><dn>I</dn> mention <dn>את</dn> Rahaḇ and Baḇel to those who know <dn>Me</dn>; See, O Philistia and Tsor, with Kush, ‘This and that one was born there.’ </dq> [5] And of Tsiyon it is said, “Each one was born in her; For the Most High <dn>Himself</dn> does establish her.” [6] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does write, In the register of the peoples, “This one was born there.” Selah. [7] And the singers and the players on instruments – All my fountains, are in you.
